# Source comparison report

Complete supplied brief/source, complete draft, and supplied quotation guidance read. This is a source comparison only. English source to Swedish draft; no external material used. The accounting below includes title, lead, body, attributed speech, link and disclosure. Negations retain the proposition’s subject, scope and attribution. Source quotations identify the supplied statement excluding each negation; where they do not exclude it, a concrete compatible counterexample is given.

## Findings requiring repair

1. **Source support: absence of a comparison becomes absence of supporting material.** Draft: “Det finns inget underlag för en jämförelse med andra leverantörer.” Source: “No comparison with another supplier is available.” These are different knowledge claims: an unavailable comparison does not establish that no basis for one exists. Counterexample: the source package could contain no completed supplier comparison, while Elm Quay has test notes permitting one. Smallest supported repair: “Någon jämförelse med en annan leverantör finns inte tillgänglig.” Keeping “i underlaget” as a scope marker is also possible: “Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med en annan leverantör.” This finding does not claim that a comparison was actually made.

2. **Source support: expansion decision becomes continuation decision.** Draft: “Innan teamet beslutar om en fortsättning ska det kontrollera hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.” Source: “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” In context the pending decision concerns expansion. “En fortsättning” can instead assert a pending decision on whether to continue the existing trial at all. Counterexample: the team has already decided to keep using the log in the original buildings but has yet to decide whether to expand it. That is compatible with the source but contradicts the draft’s broader pending continuation decision. Smallest repair: replace “en fortsättning” with “en utökning”. The supported larger-repair check and ordering should stay.

## Complete claim accounting

### Title and lead

1. Draft: “Elm Quay fick en gemensam vy över felanmälningarna”. Proposition: Elm Quay obtained a shared view of repair reports. Precise negation: Elm Quay did not obtain a shared view of repair reports. Support excluding negation: trial of a “shared repair log”, and Lind’s “Having one view of the reports helps us”. The title’s “fick” makes no stronger measured-benefit or causal claim. Supported.

2. Draft: “En gemensam vy över felanmälningarna hjälper Elm Quay Housings underhållsteam, enligt arbetsledaren Maya Lind.” Proposition: Lind says that having one view of repair reports helps Elm Quay’s maintenance team. Negation: Lind does not say that having one view of repair reports helps that team. Support excluding negation: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind” and “Having one view of the reports helps us”. This is attributed experience, not independently measured effectiveness. Supported.

3. Draft: “arbetsledaren Maya Lind” / “underhållsarbetsledaren Maya Lind”. Proposition: Maya Lind is the customer’s maintenance supervisor. Negation: Maya Lind is not the customer’s maintenance supervisor. Support excluding negation: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind”. Supported in both occurrences.

4. Draft: “Efter åtta veckors försök i två byggnader skulle hon välja att göra om det”. Proposition: Following the eight-week trial in two buildings, Lind’s assessment is that she would choose to do the trial again. Negation: Following that eight-week trial in two buildings, Lind’s assessment is not that she would choose to do the trial again. Support excluding negation: “trial ... in two buildings”; “The trial lasted eight weeks”; “I would choose to do the trial again”; source expressly describes the final quotation as her “actual, qualified assessment”. The evaluative chronology is the supplied retrospective trial assessment, not an invented interview date. Supported.

5. Draft: “men med mer tid för förberedelser”. Proposition: Lind qualifies her willingness to repeat the trial by saying she would allow more preparation time. Negation: Lind does not qualify her willingness to repeat it by saying she would allow more preparation time. Support excluding negation: “but I would leave an extra week for preparation”. Supported; “mer tid” is a faithful less-specific lead paraphrase, with the exact week retained later.

6. Draft: “Något beslut om att utöka försöket är ännu inte fattat.” Proposition: The team has not yet made its decision about expanding the trial. Negation: The team has already made its decision about expanding the trial. Support excluding negation: “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” The future decision supplies the absence of a present decision; this is not inferred solely from absence of expansion. Supported.

### Customer, selection and setup

7. Draft: “Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter.” Proposition: Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. Negation: Elm Quay Housing does not manage 640 flats. Support excluding negation: “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.” Supported.

8. Draft: “Tidigare förvarades felanmälningar via telefon och mejl separat.” Proposition: Before the trial, telephone repair reports and email repair reports were stored separately. Negation: Before the trial, those telephone and email repair reports were not stored separately. Support excluding negation: “Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately.” Supported.

9. Draft: “I september 2025 beslutade det egna underhållsteamet att prova en gemensam logg för reparationsärenden i två av byggnaderna.” Proposition: In September 2025 Elm Quay’s own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two of its buildings. Negation: In September 2025 Elm Quay’s own maintenance team did not decide to trial a shared repair log in two of its buildings. Support excluding negation: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.” All modifiers and the customer’s agency are preserved. Supported.

10. Draft quotation: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle kunna se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort.” Proposition: Lind says the team wanted the evening shift to be able to see what the morning shift had already done. Negation: Lind does not say the team wanted the evening shift to be able to see what the morning shift had already done. Support excluding negation: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done.” Supported as attributed intent, not a claim that a particular evening shift actually consulted particular reports.

11. Draft quotation: “Kategorierna tog vi fram själva”. Proposition: Lind says the team itself developed the categories. Negation: Lind does not say the team itself developed the categories. Support excluding negation: “The categories were ours”, read with “The maintenance team designed its categories”. The implicit ownership refers to customer authorship, which the supplied context settles. Supported.

12. Draft quotation: “Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”. Proposition: Lind says Svale helped the team put its categories into the log. Negation: Lind does not say Svale helped the team put its categories into the log. Support excluding negation: “Svale helped us put them into the log.” Supported.

13. Draft: “skriver ... i en mejlintervju”. Proposition: Lind supplied the quoted interview statements by email. Negation: Lind did not supply the quoted interview statements by email. Support excluding negation: “All interviews occurred by email”. The draft does not invent spoken delivery or an interview scene. Supported.

14. Draft: “Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation.” Proposition: The maintenance team selected Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show each repair’s status. Negation: The maintenance team did not select Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show each repair’s status. Support excluding negation: “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair.” Preserves the test’s question without adding a quantified test result or superiority claim. Supported.

15. Draft: “Det finns inget underlag för en jämförelse med andra leverantörer.” Proposition: No basis/material for comparison with other suppliers exists. Negation: Some basis/material for comparison with other suppliers exists. Closest source: “No comparison with another supplier is available.” This does not rule out the negation: underlying notes could exist although no comparison is available. Even if read as scoped to the supplied package, absence of a finished comparison is not identical to absence of material from which comparison could be made. Source-support finding 1; repair to absence of an available comparison.

16. Draft: “Teamet utformade kategorierna”. Proposition: The maintenance team designed the categories. Negation: The maintenance team did not design the categories. Support excluding negation: “The maintenance team designed its categories”. Supported; independently corroborates the quoted customer authorship.

17. Draft: “behöll möjligheten för de boende att felanmäla via telefon”. Proposition: The maintenance team kept telephone reporting available to residents. Negation: The maintenance team did not keep telephone reporting available to residents. Support excluding negation: “kept telephone reporting open for residents”. Supported; no invented claim of exclusive digital reporting.

18. Draft: “Svale konfigurerade loggen”. Proposition: Svale configured the log. Negation: Svale did not configure the log. Support excluding negation: “Svale configured the log”. Supported.

19. Draft: “utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen”. Proposition: Svale trained six staff during two sessions. Negation: Svale did not train six staff during two sessions. Support excluding negation: “trained six staff during two sessions”. Supported, including both figures.

20. Draft: “Lind beskriver vad förberedelserna krävde”. Proposition: Lind’s following account describes preparation effort. Negation: Lind’s following account does not describe preparation effort. Support excluding negation: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.” This introductory characterisation is limited to the actual comparative effort and recommended allocation of time; it adds no specific duration. Supported.

21. Draft quotation: “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att registrera de första anmälningarna.” Proposition: Lind says the team spent more time agreeing on categories than entering the first reports. Negation: Lind does not say the team spent more time agreeing on categories than entering the first reports. Support excluding negation: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports.” Supported; retains “first”, so the comparison does not expand to all entry work.

22. Draft quotation: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång.” Proposition: Lind says she would allocate that category-agreement time before the next building starts using the arrangement. Negation: Lind does not say she would allocate that category-agreement time before the next building starts using the arrangement. Support excluding negation: “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.” The building’s start is the source’s contextual metonymy for the trial/implementation starting there. Both versions remain conditional recommendations, not assertions that expansion is scheduled. Supported.

### Trial count and measurements

23. Draft: “Under de åtta försöksveckorna”. Proposition: The trial lasted eight weeks. Negation: The trial did not last eight weeks. Support excluding negation: “The trial lasted eight weeks.” Supported here and in the lead.

24. Draft: “registrerades 31 felanmälningar, enligt Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning”. Proposition: Elm Quay’s internal trial note reports 31 repair reports entered during the eight-week trial, with emergencies and pre-trial orders excluded from the reporting. Negation: Elm Quay’s internal trial note does not report 31 repair reports entered during the eight-week trial with those exclusions. Support excluding negation: “Elm Quay’s internal trial note ... says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.” The next draft sentence immediately supplies the exclusions; scope carried over here. Supported without claiming the count covers all repair activity.

25. Draft: “Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning daterad den 4 december 2025”. Proposition: The cited note is Elm Quay’s internal trial note dated 4 December 2025. Negation: The cited note is not Elm Quay’s internal trial note dated 4 December 2025. Support excluding negation: “Elm Quay’s internal trial note, 4 December 2025”. Supported.

26. Draft: “Akuta ärenden ... ingår inte i redovisningen.” Proposition: The trial note’s reporting excludes emergencies. Negation: The trial note’s reporting includes emergencies. Support excluding negation: “It excludes emergencies”. Supported; this is exclusion from reporting, not a claim no emergency happened.

27. Draft: “arbeten som beställts före försöket ingår inte i redovisningen.” Proposition: The trial note’s reporting excludes work ordered before the trial. Negation: The trial note’s reporting includes work ordered before the trial. Support excluding negation: “It excludes ... work ordered before the trial”. Supported; no claim such work did not exist.

28. Draft: “Mediantiden från felanmälan till tilldelning av ärendet var två arbetsdagar under försöket”. Proposition: Within the note’s trial reporting, median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial. Negation: Within that reporting, median time from report to assignment was not two working days during the trial. Support excluding negation: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial”. Supported. The earlier attribution and exclusions remain the context.

29. Draft: “jämfört med tre under den föregående åttaveckorsperioden”. Proposition: Within the cited reporting, median report-to-assignment time in the preceding eight-week period was three working days. Negation: Within that reporting, median report-to-assignment time in the preceding eight-week period was not three working days. Support excluding negation: “and three in the preceding eight-week period”. The grammatical carryover of median, report-to-assignment and working days is intact. Supported.

30. Draft: “Arbetsbelastningen skilde sig dock mellan perioderna.” Proposition: The trial and preceding eight-week period had different workloads. Negation: Those two periods did not have different workloads. Support excluding negation: “The periods had different workloads”. Supported; no invented direction or degree of workload difference.

31. Draft: “Anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden.” Proposition: The note explicitly does not attribute the observed difference in median report-to-assignment time to the software. Negation: It is not the case that the note explicitly does not attribute that observed difference to the software. Support excluding negation: “the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software”. Supported as the note’s position. The draft does not claim the software is known to have had no effect.

32. Draft: “Mätningen gäller tiden till tilldelning, inte tiden tills reparationen var färdig.” Proposition: The reported duration measures report-to-assignment time rather than repair completion time. Negation: The reported duration does not measure report-to-assignment time rather than repair completion time. Support excluding negation: “Median time from report to assignment”; “There are no ... completion-time measurements”. Supported; prevents endpoint confusion.

33. Draft: “Underlaget innehåller inga mätningar av kostnader”. Proposition: The supplied material contains no cost measurements. Negation: The supplied material contains cost measurements. Support excluding negation: “There are no cost ... measurements.” Supported with appropriately limited knowledge scope.

34. Draft: “Underlaget innehåller inga mätningar av ... boendes nöjdhet”. Proposition: The supplied material contains no resident-satisfaction measurements. Negation: The supplied material contains resident-satisfaction measurements. Support excluding negation: “There are no ... resident-satisfaction ... measurements.” Supported, and does not claim residents were dissatisfied or unaffected.

35. Draft: “Underlaget innehåller inga mätningar av ... tid till slutförd reparation.” Proposition: The supplied material contains no repair-completion-time measurements. Negation: The supplied material contains repair-completion-time measurements. Support excluding negation: “There are no ... completion-time measurements.” Supported.

### Assessment, decision and ending

36. Draft: “Linds egen bedömning rymmer både nyttan och ett förbehåll”. Proposition: Lind’s own assessment combines a stated benefit and a reservation. Negation: Lind’s own assessment does not combine a stated benefit and a reservation. Support excluding negation: “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation”; “Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures.” “Nyttan” here describes her assessment, not an independently proven or quantified effect. Supported.

37. Draft quotation: “Jag skulle välja att göra om försöket.” Proposition: Lind says she would choose to do the trial again. Negation: Lind does not say she would choose to do the trial again. Support excluding negation: “I would choose to do the trial again.” Supported. No universal supplier recommendation is implied.

38. Draft quotation: “Att ha en gemensam vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss”. Proposition: Lind says having one view of the reports helps the team. Negation: Lind does not say having one view of the reports helps the team. Support excluding negation: “Having one view of the reports helps us”. Supported attributed benefit, as in claim 2.

39. Draft quotation: “men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser”. Proposition: Lind qualifies that favorable assessment by saying she would allow an extra week for preparation. Negation: Lind does not qualify that favorable assessment by saying she would allow an extra week for preparation. Support excluding negation: “but I would leave an extra week for preparation”. Supported with precise duration and conditional stance.

40. Draft: “Försöket har ännu inte utökats.” Proposition: The trial has not yet expanded. Negation: The trial has already expanded. Support excluding negation: “The trial has not yet expanded”. Supported with warranted certainty.

41. Draft: “Innan teamet beslutar om en fortsättning”. Proposition: A decision on continuing the trial remains for the team to make. Negation: A decision on continuing the trial does not remain for the team to make. Closest source: “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs”. This supports a pending expansion decision. It does not exclude the possibility that continuing in the existing buildings has already been settled. Source-support finding 2; change “fortsättning” to “utökning”.

42. Draft: “Innan teamet beslutar om en fortsättning ska det kontrollera hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer.” Proposition: Before making the pending continuation decision, the team will check how the categories work for larger repairs. Negation: The team will not check how the categories work for larger repairs before making the pending continuation decision. Source establishes exactly that sequence for the expansion decision: “the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs”. It does not exclude a continuation decision already made before that check. Same finding 2 and same one-word repair. The check itself and its focus on larger repairs are supported and must stay.

43. Draft: “För den som vill läsa vidare finns [Svales checklista för införande](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).” Proposition: The supplied optional link at that exact URL is Svale’s implementation checklist, a document readers can read. Negation: The supplied optional link at that URL is not Svale’s implementation checklist, a document readers can read. Support excluding negation: “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read”. Supported destination description; the optional invitation is advocacy rather than a factual promise of results. The draft makes no claim that the fictional URL has been independently tested.

44. Draft: “Detta kundcase publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems”. Proposition: This customer case is supplier-published material from Svale Systems. Negation: This customer case is not supplier-published material from Svale Systems. Support excluding negation: “The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems”; “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.” Supported publication framing, not a claim that an independent news outlet published it.

45. Draft: “bygger på ett fiktivt underlag”. Proposition: This customer case is based on fictional supplied material. Negation: This customer case is not based on fictional supplied material. Support excluding negation: “SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package.” Supported disclosure.

## Translation comparison (separate from source support)

No unresolved translation finding.

- First quotation preserves the shift-specific intention, the already-completed morning work, customer authorship of categories and Svale’s assisting role. “Skulle kunna se” expresses the intended ability implicit in the shared-log purpose, without turning intention into proof of use. “Kategorierna tog vi fram själva” is settled by the accompanying explicit source fact that the team designed its categories. The language reads as idiomatic Swedish first-person speech and retains the plain, practical voice.
- Second quotation preserves comparative preparation effort, “first reports”, the conditional first-person recommendation and its timing before the next building starts. “Nästa byggnad kommer i gång” retains the source’s contextual metonymy; the surrounding trial/implementation context supplies its referent. No concrete meaning or voice obstruction warrants imposing a synonym. It does not assert an approved expansion.
- Third quotation preserves willingness to repeat, the experiential benefit attributed to Lind, the opposing “but”, first-person conditional stance and the exact extra preparation week. It does not convert her assessment into a supplier recommendation for all housing companies or an inference from the numerical comparison.

## Further implication checks

The count has no unsupported “high”, “low” or success characterisation. No claim of savings, resident delight or shorter completion time appears. Differing median assignment times are not turned into software causation in the title, lead or body. Customer agency is maintained throughout. Supplier narration stays in third person. The interview is correctly identified as email, with no invented physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue. The quotations add shift-specific intent, comparative preparation effort and the exact extra-week reservation beyond their immediate narrative framing. The final benefit quotation partially reprises the lead but still contributes the customer’s qualified first-person assessment.

## Completion status

Complete: all factual and attributed propositions in the exact complete draft have been accounted for, with scope-preserving negations and source support or source-compatible counterexamples. Two unresolved source-support findings remain (comparison availability versus absence of underlying material; expansion versus continuation). No unresolved translated-quotation finding. Smallest supported repairs are supplied above. Sources and draft were not changed.

# Fresh source and translated-quotation comparison

Scope: the complete supplied source.md, complete supplied draft.md, and supplied quotations.md were read. No other reports, outside sources, or skills were consulted. The accounting below tests assertions as written, including attribution and modifiers. A negation of an attributed assertion concerns what that source says, rather than independently denying the underlying event.

## Source passage key

S1 (brief): “Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party.”

S2 (brief): “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.”

S3 (material): “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.”

S4: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”

S5: “Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”

S6: “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.”

S7: “The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.”

S8: “Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions.”

S9: “The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”

S10: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.”

S11: “The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.”

S12: “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”

S13: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations”.

S14 (first quotation): “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

S15 (second quotation): “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

S16 (third quotation): “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

S17: “Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures.”

S18: “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”

S19: “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.”

S20 (package opening): “SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.”

In the accounting, “ruled out by S…” identifies the supplied statement that contradicts the precise negation. These identifiers resolve to the quoted passages above.

## Complete claim accounting

1. Draft heading: “Elm Quay fick en gemensam vy över felanmälningarna”. Proposition: Elm Quay acquired a shared view of its repair reports in the described trial. Negation: Elm Quay did not acquire a shared view of its repair reports in the described trial. Support: S4 describes trialling a shared log, S9 establishes actual use, and S16 expressly describes having one view. Negation ruled out by those passages together. Supported. The heading makes no claim of a company-wide rollout or measured improvement.

2. Draft: “En gemensam vy över felanmälningarna hjälper Elm Quay Housings underhållsteam, enligt arbetsledaren Maya Lind.” Proposition: Maya Lind says that having a shared view of the repair reports helps Elm Quay Housing’s maintenance team. Negation: Maya Lind does not say that having a shared view of the repair reports helps Elm Quay Housing’s maintenance team. Support: S13 identifies the speaker and S16 says “Having one view of the reports helps us”. Negation ruled out by S13/S16. Supported attributed assessment; not a measured effectiveness claim.

3. Draft: “enligt arbetsledaren Maya Lind” and “underhållsarbetsledaren Maya Lind”. Proposition: Maya Lind is the customer’s maintenance supervisor. Negation: Maya Lind is not the customer’s maintenance supervisor. Support and rule-out: S13. Supported; the Swedish role description retains the supplied responsibility.

4. Draft: “Efter åtta veckors försök i två byggnader skulle hon välja att göra om det”. Proposition: Lind’s assessment following the described eight-week trial in two buildings is that she would choose to do that trial again. Negation: Lind’s assessment following that eight-week trial in two buildings is not that she would choose to do that trial again. Support: S4 establishes the two-building scope, S9 the completed eight-week duration, and S16/S17 supply her actual qualified retrospective assessment. Negation ruled out by S4/S9/S16/S17. Supported. This is a hypothetical preference, not an assertion that another trial has been scheduled or conducted.

5. Draft: “men med mer tid för förberedelser”. Proposition: Lind’s stated preference to repeat the trial includes allowing more preparation time than in the described trial. Negation: Lind’s stated preference to repeat the trial does not include allowing more preparation time than in the described trial. Support and rule-out: S16, “but I would leave an extra week for preparation”. Supported; the introduction generalises the amount while the quotation later preserves the exact extra week.

6. Draft: “Något beslut om att utöka försöket är ännu inte fattat.” Proposition: The team has not yet decided whether to expand the trial. Negation: The team has already decided whether to expand the trial. Support and rule-out: S18 says that the team “will decide after checking” the categories for larger repairs. Supported by a positive statement of the pending decision, not merely inferred from an absence of reporting about a decision.

7. Draft: “Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter.” Proposition: Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. Negation: Elm Quay Housing does not manage 640 flats. Support and rule-out: S3. Supported without an unsupported judgement of company size or capacity.

8. Draft: “Tidigare förvarades felanmälningar via telefon och mejl separat.” Proposition: Before the trial, telephone repair reports and emailed repair reports were stored separately. Negation: Before the trial, telephone repair reports and emailed repair reports were not stored separately. Support and rule-out: S5. Supported. No delay, lost report, or other consequence is asserted.

9. Draft: “I september 2025 beslutade det egna underhållsteamet att prova en gemensam logg för reparationsärenden i två av byggnaderna.” Proposition: In September 2025, Elm Quay Housing’s own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings within its housing operation. Negation: In September 2025, Elm Quay Housing’s own maintenance team did not decide to trial a shared repair log in two buildings within its housing operation. Support and rule-out: S4 in the context of S3. Supported with the actor, decision date, experimental status, and building count intact.

10. Draft quotation: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle kunna se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort.” Proposition: Lind says that her team wanted the evening shift to be able to see work already done by the morning shift. Negation: Lind does not say that her team wanted the evening shift to be able to see work already done by the morning shift. Support and rule-out: S14 first sentence. Supported as the team’s stated intention. It does not claim that every evening worker actually accessed the information.

11. Draft quotation: “Kategorierna tog vi fram själva”. Proposition: Lind says that the categories originated with her team rather than being supplied to them by Svale. Negation: Lind does not say that the categories originated with her team rather than being supplied to them by Svale. Support: S14, “The categories were ours”, with S7 explicitly settling the origin as the team’s design. Negation ruled out by S14 read in the explicit context of S7. Supported interpretation of “ours”; no independence from all assistance is added because the adjacent clause expressly credits Svale’s assistance.

12. Draft quotation: “Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”. Proposition: Lind says Svale helped her team put the team’s categories into the log. Negation: Lind does not say Svale helped her team put the team’s categories into the log. Support and rule-out: S14 second sentence. Supported with the scope of assistance intact.

13. Draft: “skriver … Maya Lind i en mejlintervju.” Proposition: The quoted interview statements by Lind were provided in an email interview. Negation: The quoted interview statements by Lind were not provided in an email interview. Support and rule-out: S13 identifies these statements as the customer interview, and S19 states that all interviews occurred by email. Supported medium and attribution. No face-to-face scene is invented.

14. Draft: “Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation.” Proposition: The maintenance team selected Svale Systems after testing whether the log could display each repair’s status. Negation: The maintenance team did not select Svale Systems after testing whether the log could display each repair’s status. Support and rule-out: S6. Supported sequence and test scope. ## Translated-quotation comparison

### First quotation

Source: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

Draft: “Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle kunna se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna tog vi fram själva; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen”.

Assessment: meaning, stance, and certainty preserved in idiomatic Swedish. “Skulle kunna se” correctly expresses intended access, not achieved universal use. “Tog vi fram själva” renders the team’s authorship, explicitly settled by S7, while the adjacent assistance clause keeps the division of work. The direct, practical collective voice remains. No translation finding.

### Second quotation

Source: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

Draft: “Vi lade mer tid på att komma överens om kategorierna än på att registrera de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång.”

Assessment: the first sentence preserves the comparison, initial-report scope, and practical voice. The second preserves the conditional first-person recommendation and refers back to category-agreement time.

Translation finding T1: “innan nästa byggnad kommer i gång” transfers the English building-as-activity metonym into Swedish with an unclear activity. An existing building does not itself “komma i gång”; without naming the trial, the phrase can instead evoke a construction project beginning. The supplied context settles that the next building would begin participation in the log trial, and does not supply a construction project. This is a concrete referent obstruction, not a proposed synonym or a change in Lind’s advice.

Smallest supported repair: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan försöket kommer i gång i nästa byggnad.” This names the implicit trial while retaining “skulle”, “den tiden”, and Lind’s straightforward spoken register. It does not assert that expansion is approved: the recommendation remains hypothetical. No underlying source-support defect is assigned to the intended reading of the current sentence.

### Third quotation

Source: “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Draft: “Jag skulle välja att göra om försöket. Att ha en gemensam vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser.”

Assessment: the translation keeps the hypothetical choice, asserted experienced benefit, collective beneficiary, contrasting reservation, and exact extra week. “Göra om försöket” in the preceding “skulle välja” construction reads as choosing the trial again, not an assertion that it failed and must be repaired. “Gemensam vy” is ordinary interface-related language in this shared-log context and preserves the single-view meaning. No translation finding.
